See [F\_383\_prompts\_need\_to\_be\_shown\_faster.md](design/releases/0_7_0/F_383_prompts_need_to_be_shown_faster.md) where we improved the way prompts are shown in the conversation log.

I notice though there is still a visible switch between in-transmission conversation-items and the regular conversation-log-item. The in-transmission prompt disappears and then comes back as a regular prompt. why is this? how come that there is a separate 'remove' that forces a UI refresh? It looks extremely fishy, as if something is happening in between? this should not be the case, the in-transmission item should only be replaced by the actual event at the time we get the ack on the prompt. so it should be a simple replace, which it doesn't appear to be. why?

entries.content:
The “remove” is a real backend step: `agentPromptDispatched` removes the prompt from the queue **before** `sendMessage` produces an `agentUserMessage` ([action_run.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:248)). The frontend retains a pending row during that interval ([action_conversation_store.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/conversation/state/action_conversation_store.ts:239)).

The visible switch comes from rendering. Pending, queued, and sent messages are separate components in separate transcript sections ([action_conversation_transcript.tsx](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/conversation/transcript/action_conversation_transcript.tsx:125)). Each transition removes one DOM row and mounts another; it is not a replacement of the same row. The test checks that the prompt exists after each event, but does not check for a visual gap during the switch ([action_popup.test.tsx](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/components/actions/run/popup/action_popup.test.tsx:2062)).

So the extra backend event has a purpose, but the current UI structure explains the apparent disappearance. Static inspection cannot confirm whether an empty frame is painted.

This means it has been implemented incorrectly.

What is the difference between agentPromptDispatched and sendMessage
I’ll trace where `agentPromptDispatched` is emitted and where `sendMessage` produces the user message event.

entries.content:
You’re right that dispatch is **not** the acknowledgment that the agent received the prompt.

`agentPromptDispatched` means the backend has taken the prompt out of its queue and is about to send it ([action_run.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:244)). `sendMessage` then writes it to the agent; only after that succeeds does it add a user message to the conversation, persist it, and emit `agentUserMessage` ([agent_run_interactions.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_run_interactions.js:16)).

That interval explains why the queue needs a removal event. It does **not** justify making the prompt disappear from the chatlog: the pending row is meant to cover the interval. The UI still switches between separately mounted rows, which is the implementation issue identified above.
is there any other use for the `agentPromptDispatched` message?
I’ll check every producer and consumer of `agentPromptDispatched` to see whether anything depends on it beyond the queue transition.

Yes. Besides updating the chatlog’s temporary row, `agentPromptDispatched` removes the prompt from the frontend queue ([action_run_registry.ts](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/app/src/services/actions/action_run_registry.ts:929)).

It also covers **queued continuations**: the backend can take a prompt from the queue to start another agent run, without calling `sendMessage` ([action_run.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:264)). In that path, `agentPromptDispatched` tells the frontend the prompt is no longer queued. I found no other production consumer beyond the queue update and the temporary submission state update.

No. I described that path imprecisely. For a queued continuation, the backend removes the prompt from the queue, then passes its content and submission ID as the **next agent run’s input** ([action_run.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_run.js:803)). The executor sends that input when it starts the continued run ([action_agent_executor.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/action/action_agent_executor.js:114)).

So the message is sent, but through a new run rather than `sendMessage` on the current streaming run. `agentPromptDispatched` still occurs before that new run succeeds; it only means the queue has handed off the prompt.
so this means we should not remove the conversation item when we receive the `agentPromptDispatched` message, right?

Yes. `agentPromptDispatched` means the prompt has left the queue, **not** that a sent conversation entry exists. The chatlog should keep the prompt visible until `agentUserMessage`, or a matching user entry in the continued run’s `agentStarted` conversation, takes over.

The queue entry must still be removed so it can no longer be edited or sent again. The current code keeps a temporary row after dispatch, but switches from the queued row to a separately mounted pending row. That switch is what needs correction.

> or a matching user entry in the continued run’s agentStarted conversation, takes over.

this is the part i still don't understand. why do we have different paths here. it sounds like an architectural error
I’ll trace when each path creates its user message so I can explain why the frontend receives different events.

entries.content:
There are two ways to deliver a prompt because an agent turn can **start a process** or **write to an already running process**. In the start path, the backend creates the user message as part of the initial conversation and sends that conversation in `agentStarted` ([agent_runner_service.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:132)). In the live path, it writes the prompt, then emits `agentUserMessage` ([agent_run_interactions.js](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_run_interactions.js:16)).

Your architectural concern is valid at the **event contract**: the frontend has to recognize the same outcome—“this submission is now a conversation message”—in two different ways. That complicates reconciliation and makes the row switching easier to get wrong. The two delivery mechanisms have a reason to exist; exposing two different acknowledgment shapes to the chatlog is the questionable part.

so, things we need to fix:

* `The queue entry must still be removed so it can no longer be edited or sent again.`
  no, we don't need to remove it, we need to disable the edit, that is all
* `agentPromptDispatched` should not trigger a remove, just a disable on the edit
* align the event contract for 'agentUserMessage', split it from ' agentStarted'
I’ll implement those three changes: keep dispatched prompts visible but non-editable, and emit the initial user message through `agentUserMessage` so the frontend uses one acknowledgment path.

entries.content:
Implemented the three changes. `agentPromptDispatched` now keeps the prompt visible as **Sending** and disables its edit and delete controls. The row is removed when the matching `agentUserMessage` arrives. New turns now emit that user message separately from `agentStarted`, so the frontend uses the same acknowledgment path for new and live turns.

Typecheck, lint, and the focused service and desktop tests pass. The popup file has 110 passing tests, including the changed flows, and two unrelated existing failures: its project usage button expectation and a waiting-state fixture that emits a `running` update. I left those outside this change.
